question: Can observational data and one perfect intervention per hidden scalar variable identify the variables, intervention targets and causal DAG when observations are an unknown nonlinear mixture and targets are unknown? Ordinary conditional-independence discovery assumes the causal variables are already measured. The talk seeks recovery in arbitrary dimension without supplying the graph or intervention targets.
result: Under positive normalized C³ latent densities on the closed cube, shared C² invertible mixing, causal minimality, one perfect intervention per node, prescribed strict ratio-monotonicity signs and ancestral-cover separation, the coordinates, targets and DAG are identified up to separate invertible C² coordinate changes and simultaneous relabeling. Define R_i=dP^i/dP^0 and let D_ji compare the distribution of R_i under P^j and P^0. For H_D={j→i:j≠i,D_ji>0}, TC(H_D)=TC(G^π). In a recovered topological order, U_i=C_i(L_i|L_Bi), with the conditional CDF computed under P^i, satisfies U_i(f(v))=Q_π(i)(v_π(i)) for positive sign and 1−Q_π(i)(v_π(i)) for negative sign. The unique inclusion-minimal predecessor set A satisfying U_i ⟂ U_(Bi\A) | U_A under P^0 identifies the direct parents. Cover separation is open dense within every nonempty fixed-sign stratum in the relative C² topology. For fitted ratios and independent evaluation data, ε_N=2√2 a_N(η)+2{1+√[2 log(n(n+1)/α)]}/√(min_e N_e). Selecting edges with D̂_ji>ε_N yields only ancestral edges with probability at least 1−α−η; if every cover has D_ji>2ε_N, transitive closure recovers the entire ancestor order with the same guarantee.
mechanism: First compute each intervention-to-observation likelihood ratio. At X=f(v), the common observation-map factor and all unchanged causal factors cancel, leaving q_π(i)(v_π(i))/p_π(i)(v_π(i)|v_pa(π(i))). Next compare this same scalar score across environments. Draw j→i whenever intervention j changes score i’s distribution. These arrows reveal ancestry, and cover separation ensures their paths recover all ancestor relations. Choose a topological order. Earlier scores determine earlier latent variables by successive monotone inversion, so conditioning on all predecessor scores fixes the current variable’s parents. Compute the current log-score’s conditional percentile under its own intervention environment. There the target follows q independently of its predecessors, so the percentile becomes Q of the target, possibly reversed, and loses its parent dependence. Finally, use observational conditional independence among these recovered coordinates to find each variable’s minimal parent set. The sample procedure estimates ratios on training data and uses independent evaluation data to retain only discrepancies exceeding a simultaneous confidence radius.
why_true: The ratios remove the unknown mixing before any coordinates are recovered. A nonancestor intervention cannot change the joint law of a target and its parents, so it cannot change that target’s score distribution; detected arrows therefore cannot introduce false ancestry. Separating every ancestral cover supplies enough arrows to recover all ancestry through paths. Strict monotonicity makes predecessor-score inversion possible. Ranking under the target’s own intervention is essential: its parent-independent density makes the recovered percentile a function of that variable alone. Separate invertible transformations preserve conditional independence, while factorization, positivity and causal minimality identify the minimal parent sets. Minimality alone permits cancellation in score distributions. The genericity argument constructs a separating endpoint for each cover, interpolates toward it, and uses an analytic second-moment difference that is nonzero at the endpoint to obtain separation arbitrarily nearby. Stability and finitely many covers then give open dense simultaneous separation. The statistical radius accounts for ratio error and evaluation noise, so a positive lower confidence bound certifies a positive population discrepancy.
example: The worked case has 1→2 and isolated variable 3, identity mixing and known identity targets. Roots are uniform, p_2(y|x)=1+0.1(2x−1)(2y−1), and q_i(z)=4 exp(4z)/(exp(4)−1). Although R_2=q_2(y)/p_2(y|x) mixes parent and child, intervention 1 changes its distribution, revealing 1 before 2. Conditioning on L_1 fixes x; taking the conditional percentile of L_2 under intervention 2 gives U_2=Q_2(V_2). Observational pruning retains variable 1 and removes isolated variable 3 if it precedes 2. A modified parent effect supplies a cancellation example where the edge remains active but D_12=0.

findings.problem: The ancestry result has an explicit formula, but the broader identification statement, 'up to separate C² changes and relabeling,' remains verbal. Its precise meaning for two observationally equivalent latent representations is left implicit.
findings.fix: Add an equivalence formula such as Ṽ_a(x)=h_a(V_σ(a)(x)), defining σ as a permutation and each h_a as an invertible C² scalar transformation, and state that graph and target labels undergo the same permutation.

findings.problem: The specially chosen H(x) is followed by the assertion that the entire distribution of R_2 agrees across environments. The slide does not explain what this parent effect preserves, so I understand the counterexample’s implication but not its cancellation mechanism.
findings.fix: Explain the intermediate distributional invariance produced by H under the two parent laws, then connect that invariance to the unchanged mixture distribution of R_2. A short explanation or diagram would suffice.

findings.problem: 'Changes the weighting of the reciprocal child density in the score’s second moment' is the key explanation for the separating endpoint, but neither the second moment nor its difference is displayed. The numerical certificate consequently arrives without a visible object to which it applies.
findings.fix: For the positive-sign two-variable example, show E_P0[R_2²]−E_P1[R_2²]=∫∫(1−q_1(x))q_2(y)²/p_2(y|x) dy dx. Explain the weighting in words and retain the certified positive bound without deriving it.

findings.problem: The empirical MMD formula introduces ω, a new U specifying the feature map, and a change from H to ℋ. U has already denoted recovered coordinates, while these additions do not help explain the estimator.
findings.fix: Use one feature-space symbol and write D̂_ji=‖N_j⁻¹Σ_r Φ(R̂_i(X_r^(j)))−N_0⁻¹Σ_r Φ(R̂_i(X_r^(0)))‖. Omit ω and the extra U argument.
